GOALS.label: Prepare it to run without me

STEPS.text: What do you most want from the business in the next 12 months?
STEPS.why: We weight your results around this goal.

options.label: Prepare it to run without me

STEPS.text: How would your team describe the main goal for this year?
STEPS.why: If the goal is not clear to the team, effort goes in different directions.

options.label: They would all say the same thing, in similar words.
Most of them would get close.

STEPS.text: How do you decide which projects to take on?
STEPS.why: Without written priorities, the urgent usually beats the important.

options.label: Against a short, written list of priorities.
We discuss it, but nothing is written down.

STEPS.text: How often do you check progress against your plan?
STEPS.why: A plan only helps if someone looks at it.

options.label: We do not have a plan to check against.

STEPS.text: When an enquiry arrives, who replies, and how fast?
STEPS.why: Speed of reply is one of the strongest signs of whether an enquiry becomes a sale.

options.label: A named person, within the hour.
It depends on who sees it.

STEPS.text: Where are enquiries recorded?
STEPS.why: An enquiry that is not recorded cannot be followed up.

options.label: In one system the whole team uses.

STEPS.text: Do you know which channel brings your best customers?
STEPS.why: Knowing this tells you where to spend time and money.

STEPS.text: If a key person were away for two weeks, what would happen?
STEPS.why: This shows how much of the business lives in people’s heads.

options.label: Work would continue. It is written down.
Some delays, but we would manage.

STEPS.text: How are routine tasks done?
STEPS.why: Consistent work is easier to check, teach, and improve.

options.label: The same way each time, from written steps.
Mostly the same way, but nothing is written.
Each person does it their own way.
We fix problems as they happen.

STEPS.text: How much of your own week goes on day-to-day running?
STEPS.why: Time spent running the business is time not spent growing it.

STEPS.text: Does everyone know what they are responsible for?
STEPS.why: Unclear roles lead to gaps and duplicated work.

options.label: Yes. Roles are written and up to date.
Everyone does a bit of everything.

STEPS.text: How do new staff learn the job?
STEPS.why: How people are trained shapes how well the work is done.

options.label: A planned induction with written guides.
They pick it up as they go.
We rarely have time to train anyone.

STEPS.text: When someone is not performing, what happens?
STEPS.why: How this is handled affects the whole team.

options.label: We address it quickly, with clear expectations.

STEPS.text: How soon after month end do you see your figures?
STEPS.why: Late figures mean late decisions.

options.label: We do not see monthly figures.

STEPS.text: Which figures do you check every week?
STEPS.why: A few figures, checked often, beat many figures checked rarely.

options.label: A short set we agreed on.

STEPS.text: When you make a big decision, what is it based on?
STEPS.why: Good records make decisions faster and safer.

STEPS.text: A few numbers, so we can estimate what the gaps cost.
STEPS.why: Rough figures are fine. If you do not know one, say so; that tells us something too.

STEPS.text: How many people work in the business?
STEPS.why: This helps us compare you with similar businesses.

STEPS.text: What has stopped you fixing this so far?
STEPS.why: Most owners already know what needs to change. Something gets in the way.

options.label: The right skills in the team
We tried before and it did not stick

STEPS.text: How would you prefer to fix it?
STEPS.why: There is no wrong answer. It changes what we suggest next.

options.label: Have it done, working with my team

STEPS.text: When would you like to start?
STEPS.why: This helps us suggest a realistic next step.

STEPS.text: Who makes the final decision on work like this?
STEPS.why: So we know who should be part of the conversation.

options.label: Me, with a partner or family

STEPS.text: If the next 90 days went well, what would be different?
STEPS.why: Optional. A sentence or two is plenty.
STEPS.ph: For example: every enquiry gets a reply the same day, and I take a week off.

NUMS.label: Average value of a sale or order
NUMS.help: Roughly what a typical customer spends in one purchase.

NUMS.label: New enquiries in a typical month
NUMS.help: Calls, messages, emails, and walk-ins from people who might buy.

NUMS.label: Of every 10 enquiries, how many become customers?
Hours a week you spend on day-to-day running
NUMS.help: Approving, chasing, fixing, and answering questions.

direction.diy: Write the one goal for the next 12 months in a single sentence. Share it with the team this week and ask each person how their work supports it.
direction.help: A Review to set priorities with figures, then monthly check-ins until the plan runs on its own.

customers.diy: Name one person to own every enquiry. For 30 days, log each one with the date, source, reply time, and outcome.
customers.help: A Project to set up a simple CRM and a reply routine your team will use.

operations.diy: Pick the three tasks that go wrong most often. Write the steps for each on one page, and have the person who does them check it.
operations.help: A Review of how work moves through the business, then a Project to remove the steps that slow it down.

people.diy: Write a five-line role for each person: what they own, what they decide, and who they report to. Go through it with each of them.
people.help: Clear roles, a hiring plan for gaps, and training on new ways of working.

information.diy: Choose five figures to see every Monday: sales, enquiries, cash in the bank, money owed to you, and one figure for your biggest bottleneck.
information.help: A Project to build a simple monthly dashboard from the records you already have.
